title: 进化生物学 Day 16：人类的演化

questions.question: 那张「从弓背的猿到直立的人」的排队图，在「站起来」和「脑子变大」的关系上画错了什么？
options: 站起来与脑子变大同步推进，每一步都相互促进
脑子先变大，祖先变聪明后才学会站起来走路
直立行走其实出现得比图上晚得多，是脑子变大之后才有的产物
走路定型时脑子仍与黑猩猩相当，两百多万年后才变大
questions.explanation: 约 366 万年前的莱托里脚印已有足弓、大脚趾并排，露西的骨盆和膝盖已适合走路，脑子却只有四百多毫升。排队图把「后来发生」画成了「一起发生」，两者之间隔着两百多万年。
questions.question_en: The famous 'march of progress' image, from stooped ape to upright human, gets what wrong about standing up and brain enlargement?
options_en: Standing upright and brain growth advanced in lockstep, each step reinforcing the other
Brains grew first, and ancestors learned to walk upright once they got smarter
Upright walking arose much later than shown, as a consequence of bigger brains
Upright walking was established while brains were still chimp-sized; brains only began growing over two million years later
questions.explanation_en: The 3.66-million-year-old Laetoli footprints show an arch and an in-line big toe, and Lucy's pelvis and knee were built for walking, yet her brain was just over 400 ml. The picture draws 'later' as 'at the same time'; the gap between the two exceeds two million years.

questions.question: 人类演化回头看像一条从古到今的直线。为什么说这是一种误读？
options: 化石太少，其实每个时期确实只有一种人，只是我们找不全过渡类型
直线是对的，只是各物种接替的年代被估计得太早
别的支系都断了才剩一条；约六万年前至少五种人并存且有混血
因为智人更聪明，必然取代其他人种，所以直线描述大体正确
questions.explanation: 尼安德特人、丹尼索瓦人、弗洛勒斯人、吕宋人与智人曾并存，非洲之外的人至今带着一到二成的尼安德特人基因（百分之一到二）。分岔断掉后，唯一的幸存者回头看就像主干——幸存名单不是优秀名单；「我们更聪明所以赢了」几乎没有直接证据。
questions.question_en: Looking back, human evolution resembles a single line from past to present. Why is this a misreading?
options_en: Fossils are scarce, but each era really did have only one kind of human; we just haven't found all the transitional forms
The line is correct; it's just that the succession dates have been estimated too early
It looks like a line only because the other branches died out; about 60,000 years ago at least five kinds of human coexisted and interbred
Since Homo sapiens was smarter, it inevitably replaced the others, so the line is broadly right
questions.explanation_en: Neanderthals, Denisovans, Homo floresiensis and the Luzon species overlapped with Homo sapiens, and people outside Africa still carry 1–2% Neanderthal DNA. Once the branches are cut, the survivor looks like the trunk in hindsight — a survivor list is not an excellence list — and 'we won because we were smarter' has little direct evidence.

questions.question: 直立人牙齿变小、肠道相对变短等变化约在 190 万年前出现，而最早被广泛接受的用火证据约在 100 万年前。对「食物在体外加工过」这条解释，比较负责任的态度是？
options: 肠道缩短把能量让给大脑的跨物种证据已经很充分，用火时间并不重要
线索有力但时间接不上，应把缺口摆明，而且加工未必靠火
既然解剖变化指向 190 万年前，就可以推定那时已经在用火
时间对不上就说明这条解释是错的，应该放弃
questions.explanation: 加热能让食物省嚼、好吸收，生食者调查也显示纯生食很难维持体重；但近百万年的空档不该拿推断去填。2016 年实验显示，用石器切肉、捶块茎也能大幅减少咀嚼。至于「肠道让位给脑」，跨上百种哺乳动物的比较并没找到它预言的此消彼长。
questions.question_en: Homo erectus's smaller teeth and relatively shorter gut appear around 1.9 million years ago, while the oldest widely accepted evidence of fire is about 1 million years old. What is the responsible stance toward the idea that food was processed outside the body?
options_en: Cross-species evidence that the gut shrank to fund the brain is already solid, so the date of fire hardly matters
The clue is strong but the timing doesn't join up; keep the gap in view, and note that processing needn't have meant fire
Since the anatomy points to 1.9 million years ago, we can infer fire was in use by then
The mismatch shows the explanation is wrong and should be abandoned
questions.explanation_en: Heat makes food easier to chew and digest, and raw-food surveys show how hard it is to keep weight on raw diets, but a gap of nearly a million years shouldn't be filled by inference. A 2016 experiment showed that slicing meat and pounding tubers with stone tools also cuts chewing substantially. As for gut-for-brain, a comparison across over a hundred mammal species didn't find the predicted trade-off.
